items.text: Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year on year, against analyst expectations of about $109.3 billion. Adjusted EPS was $2.68 versus an expected $2.47. It guided Q4 revenue to about $130 billion (plus or minus 3%) against a roughly $125 billion consensus. The outlook assumes no data-center compute revenue from China. Interim CEO Colette Kress, in her first report since Huang's exit, raised the fiscal 2028 growth outlook to about 75% from 70%. The shares closed down 0.4% but rose roughly 2–5% after hours.
items.notes: Reports differ on the size of the after-hours gain: Yahoo/Benzinga says about 2%, Kaohoon about 5%, and Stock Titan 4.8%. The figures come from company results as relayed by outlets. Nvidia's own press release was not read.

items.text: Nvidia board chairman Harvey Jones said on the results day that the board will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and is searching for a permanent replacement. He declined to discuss the investigation into Huang's departure. This cuts against the FT-reported campaign by Silicon Valley allies for Huang's return.
items.notes: Two outlets report it consistently. No direct board statement was read.

items.text: The Pan American Health Organization formally announced on Nov 17 that the US has lost the measles-elimination status it has held since 2000, after one strain circulated for more than 12 months. CDC figures show 5,412 cases in 2026 and 48 outbreaks, and states report 10 deaths. CDC, HHS, PAHO and five public-health groups (ASTHO, APHL, BCHC, CSTE, NACCHO) issued a joint statement pledging to regain the status, citing about $100 million in extra funding to states and a decline in kindergarten MMR coverage to about 92–93%. HHS Secretary Kennedy said on X that the US will work to regain the status and that he still recommends the MMR vaccine.
items.notes: The CDC joint statement includes a quote from PAHO Director Barbosa. The PAHO page itself was not read. A Sight Magazine headline says Mexico and Bolivia also lost their status, but the article could not be fetched (unverified). KVIA, Stateline and CNN pages were blocked.

items.text: The White House withdrew Heidi Overton's nomination as FDA commissioner on Tuesday evening, hours before the Senate HELP Committee was due to vote on Nov 18. ABC cites sources saying several Republican senators objected to her positions on abortion, vaccines and vaping. BioSpace notes her backing for Trump's August order seeking separate single-disease measles, mumps and rubella shots. The FDA has had no permanent commissioner since Marty Makary left in May, and Kyle Diamantas remains acting commissioner. Semafor floated Sen. Roger Marshall as a possible replacement.
items.notes: Axios broke the story and a White House official confirmed it to ABC and The Hill. The Hill page could not be fetched. The Marshall replacement idea is Semafor's, reported via BioSpace.

items.text: NSANet, the NSA's classified internal communications network, suffered an outage on Nov 17, first reported by CNN. The NSA called it temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance and said mission-critical capabilities stayed operational. Secretary of State and NSA adviser Rubio said there was zero evidence that hackers or hostile actors were behind the recent disruptions. DNI Jay Clayton blamed simultaneous upgrades and patching across government and industry. Sen. Mark Warner said the evidence so far points to legitimate security work but the incidents still need investigating. Markets reacted badly to the initial report.
items.notes: The outage is confirmed by the NSA. The cause is the NSA's own claim and has not been independently verified. It comes days after the FAA ground stop, which also had no confirmed cause.

items.text: US stocks fell on Tuesday. CNBC figures relayed by Stock Titan show the Dow down 1.64% (more than 800 points), the Nasdaq down 0.74% and the S&P 500 down about 1%, its lowest close since late July. Traders sold chips ahead of Nvidia's results, and the CNN report of the NSA network outage also weighed. Home Depot fell 2.5% after naming a new CEO and reporting Q3 results.
items.notes: Index point levels were not given. The CNBC live page could not be fetched. The Home Depot CEO name is not confirmed, because the press release found was from 2025.

items.text: Iran's IRGC launched a third drone attack in five days on a US-operated radar at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa air base. CENTCOM said the drones were intercepted with no damage or casualties. Hours later, a US official told Al Jazeera that US strikes hit a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz. A local Iranian official said no civilian areas were damaged. Kuwait reported hostile drone attacks without naming a source. AP says Washington is weighing a return to all-out strikes or a tighter blockade, while Qatari mediation remains stalled.
items.notes: The Qeshm strike rests on an unnamed US official speaking to Al Jazeera and on Iranian local officials. The AP version (Boston Globe) did not report any US retaliation. CENTCOM confirmed the intercept.

items.text: Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday evening after more than 18 hours of travel, for the ASEAN–US special summit and talks with President Marcos at Malacañang on Wednesday. At the summit he said US–Philippine ties are closer than ever because of his personal relationship with Marcos, told ASEAN leaders to call him when there is a problem, and pointed to proposals for more joint special-forces training. He again suggested a meeting with Kim Jong Un could happen. Next he goes to APEC in Shenzhen, where the Kremlin and Beijing say a first-ever Trump–Xi–Putin trilateral meeting is set for Nov 19.
items.notes: The outcome of the Marcos bilateral meeting was not yet reported in the sources read. The trilateral date was confirmed by Peskov on Nov 14 (Anadolu: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/eurasia/kremlin-says-putin-xi-trump-to-hold-trilateral-meeting-in-shenzhen-on-nov-19/4125290). The Quad leaders' meeting in Manila is left to the US–India desk. NBC, CNN and Philstar pages were blocked or errored.

items.text: On the sidelines of the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila, Trump and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul signed a joint trade statement. Trump said a formal agreement would be finalised in the coming weeks and that Thailand would eliminate tariffs on US exports and buy $2.6 billion of US farm products.
items.notes: The terms come from Trump's account in the ABC live blog. No Thai government or USTR text was found.

items.text: Bloomberg reports that Anthropic is guiding its IPO to price at or above the top of its $70–78 range, with orders near seven times the shares on offer. The WSJ says pricing could exceed $80. At $78 the deal would raise about $90.4 billion, counting a $26 billion private placement, at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion. Books closed at 4 p.m. ET on Nov 17. Pricing is expected Nov 18 and Nasdaq trading (ANT) Nov 19.
items.notes: Based on unnamed sources. Bloomberg is paywalled and was not read directly. CNBC reports the same (page not fetchable).

items.text: US District Judge Julia Kobick in Boston blocked two August DHS directives that had narrowed curricular practical training (CPT) for foreign students to training required of every student in a programme. She found them likely arbitrary and capricious because DHS did not acknowledge it was changing a long-standing interpretation. The suit was brought by groups including the Association of American Universities. About 140,000 student-visa holders were authorised for CPT in 2024. DHS declined to comment.
items.notes: Law360 (link2) is paywalled and was not read.

items.text: Peltola now has 141,637 first-choice votes (49.98%) to Sen. Dan Sullivan's 130,162 (45.93%), about 52 votes short of an outright majority, with AP estimating 98% counted. Sullivan's campaign broke its silence on Facebook, saying it would let the count run to certification and would have more to say by the end of the week. Overseas ballots are due Nov 18, when the final count and any ranked-choice tabulation are scheduled. Certification is targeted for Nov 25.
items.notes: Unofficial Division of Elections figures relayed by Newsweek. The tabulation itself had not happened by the time of this sweep (it falls on Alaska's Nov 18).

items.text: Ahead of the Dec 11 funding deadline, Sens. Bennet, Sanders, Van Hollen and Duckworth say they will oppose any stopgap that lets Iran-war funding continue, and Sen. Tim Kaine is drafting language to block it. On the House side, several Republicans say they will block Trump's $350 billion defense reconciliation package unless the White House takes a tougher line on Russia. House and Senate Armed Services leaders meet twice this week on a compromise NDAA, after a $1.15 trillion request.
items.notes: HNGN is a secondary aggregator. These points were not cross-checked with Roll Call, AP or Politico.

items.text: NASA said Terra, the flagship Earth Observing System satellite launched in December 1999 for a six-year mission, will stop collecting science data on Dec 1 after 27 years because its systems are ageing and its orbit is drifting. The team will use its remaining fuel to lower the orbit and power it off in January 2027. Its archive (MODIS, ASTER, MISR, CERES, MOPITT) stays freely available.
items.notes: NASA's post names no successor missions and gives no budget context.
